transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I… I came because something’s been happening at work, mostly. I keep hearing people talking about me, like through the conference room walls, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s off. It’s usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company.

And it’s not like a vague thing, it sounds clear. Clear enough that I’ll answer them, and then everyone looks at me like… like they didn’t hear anything. Which is ridiculous, because those conference rooms have terrible insulation anyway—I’ve complained about that before, but facilities never prioritizes the right things. But yes, that’s why I’m here. It’s gotten hard to ignore.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or broadcasted so others can hear them?

I don’t… I don’t think of it that way, exactly. Like, I know what I’m thinking is mine, most of the time. I’m not sitting there thinking someone typed it into my head or pulled it out like a file from a server.

Broadcasted… I mean, people seem to know things sometimes, but that could be because of meetings, emails, assistants talking—companies leak information constantly. That’s just how organizations are. So I don’t know. I wouldn’t say my thoughts are being broadcast, no.

Have you ever felt like your thoughts are not your own, like someone is putting thoughts into your head or taking them away, or that your thoughts are being heard by others without you speaking them out loud?

I mean… not really in that specific way. My thoughts feel like my thoughts. I don’t sit there thinking, “Oh, that came from someone else,” or that somebody took one away.

The being heard part is… I don’t know. People in offices hear things all the time, even when you don’t mean them to, especially with glass walls and everyone pretending not to listen. At my old desk, you could hear the printer from two departments over, and they still acted like the layout was “innovative.” But if you mean thoughts without me saying anything—no, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed that, exactly.
Have you ever felt that your actions or behaviors were being controlled by some outside force or influence that you couldn’t control?

Controlled? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I make my own decisions, even if people second-guess them constantly.

Although “outside influence” is a funny phrase, because in a company everything is influence—boards, investors, legal, finance people sending memos at 11 p.m. like that’s normal. And then you have to respond, and later they act surprised that decisions were made quickly. That’s not control exactly, it’s just… pressure.

But if you mean like something taking over my body or making me do things, no. I haven’t noticed that.
Have you ever felt like people are talking about you or sending you messages through things like TV shows, radio broadcasts, or other media—even if it’s not direct voices?

TV or radio? No, I don’t think so. I mean, media is always full of messaging—branding, PR campaigns, little phrases that show up everywhere once some consultant decides it “tests well.” I notice patterns like that because that was part of my work, you know, watching how people communicate.

But if you mean, like, a show is secretly talking to me personally or sending me a message… no. I haven’t really had that. Sometimes something feels oddly relevant, but that happens to everyone, doesn’t it? You’re thinking about buying a car and suddenly every ad is a car. That’s algorithms, not… whatever you’re asking.
Have you ever felt that certain events, actions, or objects in your environment were specifically directed at you or had a special personal meaning for you, even if others might not see it that way?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I notice things, obviously—everybody does. Like if the same kind of car keeps showing up in the parking lot, or someone leaves a mug in the conference room with a slogan on it, you can start wondering why people choose what they choose.

But specifically directed at me? No, I don’t think so. I mean, workplaces are full of little signals—who gets invited to which meeting, where people sit, who suddenly stops replying to emails. That can feel personal because business is personal, no matter what anyone says. They pretend it’s all process and policy, but it’s people making choices.

So… special meaning? Not really. More like I notice patterns and sometimes I overthink whether they matter. But I wouldn’t say objects or events are meant for me in some hidden way.

Have you ever believed something was happening or being directed at you that others didn’t seem to notice, even though you didn’t necessarily think it was impossible, like a subtle form of surveillance or a hidden agenda in your workplace?

I don’t know. I mean… in a workplace, especially at my level, there are always hidden agendas. That’s not paranoia, that’s Tuesday. People have side conversations, they copy legal without telling you, they “circle back” after already making the decision somewhere else.

Surveillance, though—if you mean like someone literally watching me in a secret way, I don’t think I’ve had that. There were times I wondered why certain things got repeated back to me so quickly, like I’d say something in one meeting and then someone from another department would be acting like they already knew. But companies leak. Assistants talk, board members talk, people forward emails when they shouldn’t.

So… I guess I’ve wondered about agendas, sure, but not in some impossible way. More just office politics, and I’ve dealt with plenty of that.
Have you ever believed, even secretly to yourself, that someone was spying on you or actively working against you in ways that aren’t explained by normal office politics or leaks?

I don’t… I don’t think so. Not beyond the usual kind of maneuvering people do. I mean, “actively working against you” can mean a lot of things, right? Because sometimes someone is smiling in a meeting and then suddenly the budget has moved or the decision got made without you, and that’s not exactly friendly.

But if you mean something outside of that—like spying on me in some hidden way, or some organized thing I couldn’t explain—no, I don’t have a clear example of that. I’ve wondered about motives, sure. I used to read people’s pauses too much sometimes, like why did she say it that way, why did he look at his phone right then. But then you get into leadership training and they tell you to watch body language, and then everyone acts like you’re strange for noticing it.

So… no, not really. Not spying, I guess. More just people being people.
Have you ever had the experience of hearing your own thoughts spoken out loud as you’re thinking them, or feeling like your thoughts are being taken away or put into your mind by someone else?

I don’t think so. I mean, thoughts are already sort of “loud” sometimes, aren’t they? Like when you’re trying to answer emails and also remember whether you paid the contractor and then someone walks in asking about a quarterly number—your mind is just… talking over itself.

But hearing them spoken out loud, like an actual voice in the room? No, I haven’t noticed that. And thoughts being taken away or put in by someone else… I don’t know exactly what that would feel like. I’ve had times where I lose my train of thought, especially if people interrupt me, which happens constantly in meetings because nobody waits anymore. But that’s not someone taking it, I don’t think.

So, no—not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think.

Have you ever had the experience where it felt like your thoughts were being inserted into your mind by someone else, removed from your mind, or that your thoughts were being broadcast out loud for others to hear, even if you weren’t speaking them?

I don’t think so. I mean, not in that exact way. Thoughts being “broadcast” sounds very… I don’t know, like there would be a clear moment where everyone turns and reacts, and I haven’t had that.

Sometimes I’ll feel like people know what I’m going to say before I say it, but that’s usually because I’ve been in enough meetings where you can see the decision already happened before the discussion starts. That happens all the time in leadership spaces—people act surprised, but the document was probably circulated the night before, or someone had a dinner, or whatever.

Inserted or removed… I lose my train of thought, sure. Especially when there are too many people talking, or someone interrupts right when I’m about to make a point. But I wouldn’t say someone is putting thoughts in my head. I don’t really know what that would feel like. So… no, I haven’t noticed that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports clear auditory hallucinations involving voices commenting on them and perceiving external origin, without full realization of their pathological nature. Delusions are not clearly present, and the clinical picture is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder, where a single system of delusion (related to workplace conspiracies and surveillance) is present without prominent hallucinations outside of the delusional context. Schizophrenia and brief psychotic disorder were considered but ruled out due to absence of hallmark features such as formal thought disorder, negative symptoms, or polymorphic psychotic symptoms without a central theme.
